beliefs: f is even: f(-x)=f(x) to within noise [E1, E2, E3]
For |x| >= ~1, f is essentially linear: f(x) ≈ 16.79·|x| [E1, E2, E3]
The linear slope is slightly sublinear at very large |x|: f(127)=2131.6 vs 16.79·127=2132, f(128)=2151.2 vs 2149 [E1]
There is a special interval roughly |x| < 1 where f deviates from the linear law, with a dip near x=0 [E3, E4]
Inside |x|<1 the function is mostly monotone increasing but with a small dip/plateau near x≈0.04-0.08 and x≈0.15-0.22 (values ~0.3-0.5), then rises smoothly to meet the linear law at |x|=1 [E3, E4]
The near-zero region is noisy/erratic (e.g. f(0.1)=1.65 vs f(0.15)=0.33), so exact values there are unpredictable; only the envelope is captured [E3, E4]
The transition from the near-zero dip to the linear regime happens around |x|≈0.5-1 [E3, E4]
notes: E4 shows the near-zero region is mostly a smooth monotone rise (not a symmetric quadratic dip), with a small erratic dip near 0.04-0.08 and 0.15-0.22. Replaced the x^1.5 ramp with a smoother monotone ramp that better matches E4's envelope, keeping the erratic near-zero caveat.
